2. The prosecution case, in short, is that P.W.5 S.M.A. Mahmud, the Project Implementation Officer (hereinafter described as the PIO.), Shyamnagar in the District of Satkhira lodged a complaint before the U.N.O., Shyamnagar alleging that accused appellant G.M. Nowsher Ali as the Chairman of Gabura Union Parishad and as Chairman of the Project Committees of 12 schemes under Rainy Season Food for Work Programme, 1985 for the Gabura Union Parishad received 250 maunds of wheat for the said project but he misappropriated 93.22 maunds of wheat for which he could not furnish any explanation nor did he submit any Master Roll in proof of utilization of the wheat in question. This misappropriation was detected when the P.I.O. along with the serveyor concerned took physical measurement of the works of the project. The T.N.O. thereafter sent the matter to the Officer-in-charge of Shyamnagar Police Station for starting a regular case against the accused persons in pursuance of which Shyamnagar P.S. Case No. 5 dated 10.4.85 was started. 

 30. From the scrutiny of the evidence of the witnesses examined by the contending parties, it is found that accused Nowsher Ali admittedly lifted 175 maunds of wheat against 8 projects in question. This has been proved by both oral and documentary evidence and this fact is not also disputed by the defence. The defence plea is that the accused persons have duly completed the works of the projects and they did not misappropriate any wheat. In support of their contention the accused persons examined three witnesses who appear to be interested and hired witnesses to help the defence. The learned Divisional Special Judge was perfectly justified in rejecting their evidence on sound reasoning’s. The Master Roll for the projects in question could be a very important documentary evidence to show that the works of the projects in question were duly performed and the wheat in question was fully utilized and the accused did not misappropriate any wheat as alleged by the prosecution. It is unfortunate that the defence chose not to produce the Master Roll even before the court in proof of its plea of full utilization of the wheat in question, even though the defence examined 3 witnesses to substantiate its case. Non-production of the Master Roll, in the facts of the case, must be held to be accentuated by malafides which renders the defence case unacceptable. In the face of admitted entrustment of the wheat in question to accused appellant Nowsher Ali as the Chairman of the projects committee a heavy duty was cast upon him to account for the entrusted wheat by producing the Master Roll in proof of full utilization of the wheat but the appellant miserably failed to discharge that burden in any way whatsoever. The evidence adduced by the prosecution is so convincing and overwhelming that it excludes all reasonable hypothesis of innocence of the accused persons. 

 31. Although under our system of criminal jurisprudence the burden of proving the guilt of the accused lies ordinarily squarely on the prosecution and it does not ordinarily shift on to the accused, yet in anti-corruption cases under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, certain burden has been thrust upon the accused to account for the goods and properties entrusted to him. In our case under review, I am constrained to hold that the defence miserably failed to discharge that onus to dispel the effect of the overwhelming evidence on record proving the guilt of the accused appellant beyond all reasonable doubts. For the reasons stated above, I do not find any substance in the appeal and accordingly it fails.
